opportunity: A pointer-width value the program uses only as an array of one element type -- a parameter indexed byte by byte, the buffer malloc returned, a global that holds an allocated table, a constant table in .data read with a computed index -- is declared long or void * (or not at all), so every access prints as an integer sum behind casts: *(char *)((long)v6 + (long)v8), *(unsigned char *)((long)v1 + 0x4020). TypeOpIntAdd votes an integer for both operands of p + i and refuses to carry the loaded element's pointer back over the add (typeop.cc:1217).
test_name: tests/stages/kuna-elemptr.xml (9 assertions, pass 1 option elemptr off, pass 2 on) + 7 unit tests (p5_types/kuna_elemptr/tests.rs) + compiled round trip decompile_all_cli.rs an_element_pointer_round_trips_through_the_printed_c (fixture elemptr_x86_64.c: gcc -O0, clang -O0, gcc -O2; option on and off; gcc and clang) + tests/cli elemptr-declares-an-indexed-buffer-a-char-pointer.json, elemptr-names-an-indexed-data-table-an-array.json
inspiration: IDA prints a base64 decoder's table lookup as *((char *)ptr + *(unsigned __int8 *)(a1 + v9)), its output store as v26[v12] = BYTE2(v19) with _BYTE *v26, and the table build as *((_BYTE *)ptr + byte_5020[i]) = i: the element type comes from the access, and a constant table read with a computed index is a named array (IDA at coreutils ls -O0 main: dword_205E0[sub_FE17(...)], sort -O2 0x9120: byte_1D740[(unsigned char)*v2], gzip -O0 0x4677: word_BD000[dword_1A084 + 0x8000]).
